sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by confocal imaging at cell-cell junctions (VE-cadherin co-labelling) in HUVEC; no phosphatase activity or signalling assay reported for the N-terminally tagged construct.
sites.rationale: PTPRJ is a type-I transmembrane receptor with signal peptide 1-35 (mature N-terminus at residue 36) and a single extracellular face spanning residues 36-971; the only extracellular terminus is the mature N-terminus, placing the tag uniquely at insert_after_residue=35. Python lookup confirms residue 35 = C (last SP residue) and residue 36 = A (first mature residue), 936 residues from the TM boundary. L7 and L8 directly demonstrate surface display of human DEP1-HA in HUVEC; L1 provides indirect murine corroboration (FLAG between Ala38/Ala39 'after the signal sequence' of murine CD148). Human DEP1 (PTPRJ) carrying an N-terminal HA-tag (DEP1-HA) was expressed in confluent HUVEC cells and detected at cell-cell junctions by confocal imaging. No residue number is stated; PTPRJ is a type-I single-pass receptor with signal peptide 1-35 and a single extracellular N-terminus beginning at residue 36, so the junction is uniquely determined by topology. A second clip (L8) confirms the same construct co-expressed with SDC2-SNAP in HUVEC. An indirect murine precedent (L1) places a FLAG tag between Ala38 and Ala39 of murine CD148 'after the signal sequence', consistent with an N-terminal extracellular position.

sources.claim:
Statistical analysis was performed by one-way ANOVA with Sidak’s multiple comparison test (panels c, d), and by unpaired t-student test (panel f), (N.S. not significant, * P<0.05, ** P <0.01, *** P<0.001).

a , confocal image of confluent HUVEC cells in basal conditions showing human DEP1 carrying N-terminal HA-tag (DEP1-HA, red) expression at cell-cell junctions labeled with VE-cadherin (cyan), white arrows, lower panels.

literature_notes: L2, L3, L4, L5, and L6 all describe a C-terminally HA-tagged full-length CD148 construct. L5 explicitly confirms that permeabilization was required for anti-HA staining, proving the HA tag is intracellular (cytoplasmic C-terminus). L4 shows the tagged protein reaches the cell membrane and L3 shows CD148 retains EGFR-inhibitory function, but because the tag is intracellular these clips do not qualify a surface tag site and the position is recorded in other_positions instead. L1 (murine FLAG at Ala38/Ala39) is an indirect ortholog citation; the human equivalent junction is insert_after_residue=35 by topology, already captured by the direct human evidence in L7/L8, so no separate site is added for L1.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal HA tag on full-length CD148; permeabilization required for anti-HA immunostaining, confirming the tag is on the cytoplasmic tail and is not accessible from the extracellular face.
